lines.caption: This is a tour of the pull request for issue 96: keyboard focus stays in the pane you dragged from.
lines.say: This is a tour of the pull request for issue ninety-six: keyboard focus stays in the pane you dragged from.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
A drop from one pane onto the other no longer moves the keyboard or the active pane to the drop pane.
You drag a file from the right pane and drop it on the left pane.
The drop handler sees the drag came from the other pane, and focuses the source pane instead.
The move or copy job runs exactly as before.
When it finishes, the dropped files are selected in the left pane, without taking the focus.
Drops from another app, or within one pane, still focus the drop pane.
Paste, New Folder and rename still focus the new item through their own code path.
And Insert, from issue 95, never moved focus, which the test now checks too.
lines.say: And Insert, from issue ninety-five, never moved focus, which the test now checks too.

lines.caption: Before, a drop made the left pane active, so the next key acted on the pane you dropped on.
Focus moved twice, on the drop and when the job finished. Both now check for a drag from the other pane.
That also hands focus back when a spring-loaded folder switched panes during the drag.
Shift+Insert and Ctrl+Insert are Paste and Copy, so they're unchanged too.
lines.say: Shift Insert and Control Insert are Paste and Copy, so they're unchanged too.

lines.caption: The new helper is a three-part test on the source of the drag.
The source must be a Thunar view in the same window.
And it must sit in a different tab notebook, which means the other pane.
Drops on the other pane's tab label never switched panes, so they needed no change.
The PR changes one source file, adds one verify script, and adds this page and its narration.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
The test repeats the owner's own steps from the issue.
It borrows the first-row position from another test, and checks Insert from issue 95 alongside.
lines.say: It borrows the first-row position from another test, and checks Insert from issue ninety-five alongside.

lines.caption: In a cloud container, as CI does it, the build passed, the packages installed, and 15 of 15 tests passed.
lines.say: In a cloud container, as CI does it, the build passed, the packages installed, and fifteen of fifteen tests passed.

lines.caption: The new test showed focus staying in the source pane after a drop and after Insert, and New Folder still focusing its folder.
Drops from other apps, Shift+Insert, Ctrl+Insert and tab-label drops were not tested.
lines.say: Drops from other apps, Shift Insert, Control Insert and tab-label drops were not tested.

lines.caption: CI and the screenshot audit haven't run yet; they run after the push.
It isn't certain the local run included the last commit, so CI's run is the one to trust.
A fresh review agent found three problems, and two were fixed.
The test's drag was sped up, and a spring-loaded folder no longer leaves focus in the drop pane.
An older risk, a source view freed during a long transfer, was left for a possible follow-up.
CI's own review hasn't run yet.
A real mouse drag on the owner's desktop only happens once the owner installs the next build.
The changes, CI's comments with the screenshots, and the issue are all linked here.
Part 3. What comes later.
No open issue depends on this one yet, but the batch moves on to the split view work once it merges.
Issues 40 and 41 change the split position, and don't use this fix.
lines.say: Issues forty and forty-one change the split position, and don't use this fix.

lines.caption: Issue 16, rename in place, must keep this focus fix working.
lines.say: Issue sixteen, rename in place, must keep this focus fix working.

lines.caption: And a weak reference to the drag's source view is a possible follow-up, not filed yet.
In short: after a drop on the other pane, your keyboard stays where you were working.
